2. Heard on admission.
The appeal is admitted for hearing.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is heard finally and is decided as below.

3. This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants/claimants seeking compensation for the death of deceased (Ajit Prajapati) who died in a motor accident dated 18.04.2019 challenge impugned award dated 27.02.2024 passed by 9th MACT, District Rewa in Claim Case MVC No.848/2019 [Ramkishore Prajapati and others Vs.
Ravendra Prajapati and others] whereby compensation of Rs.10,39,200/- has been awarded.

4 . It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that learned NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:6707 2 MA-4195-2024 Tribunal has taken per month income of deceased at Rs.6,000/- as per Para 22 of the award, whereas on the date of death i.e.16.06.2021 the minimum wages of deceased was Rs.7,700/- which is not disputed by learned counsel for the Insurance Company being a legal position, however, he has otherwise supported the impugned award.

Therefore, as per minimum wage, the monthly income of the deceased on the date of accident/death was Rs.7,700/- .
5. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company does not dispute that minimum wages as on the date of accident was Rs.7,700/-.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Taking into consideration, this Court is of the considered view that less amount of compensation has been awarded.
7. As stated above, it is prima-facie established that the learned Tribunal failed to fix compensation as required under law.
Let it be remembered that strict rule of evidence is not required in motor accident claim cases.
Therefore, it seems that less amount has been paid on the basis of wrong calculation.
Therefore, the calculation by the Tribunal is erroneous.

Therefore, the total amount of enhancement after taking minimum wages according to monthly income at Rs.7,700/-, the correct calculation of the amount would be as below:-
1

Monthly Income Rs.7,700/-
2
Annual income Rs.92,400/-

personal living expenses (Rs.1,29,360/- - Rs.64,680/-
6 Multiplier considering age of deceases was 18 18 years 7 Compensation 18 as age Rs.11,64,240/-
(Rs. Rs.64,680/-x 18) 8

(2xRs.48,000/-) 9

Towards funeral expenses + Loss of estate Rs.36,000/-
(Rs.18,000/- + Rs.18,000/-) 10
Thus, the total compensation to which claimants are entitled is Rs.12,96,240/-
Since, the Tribunal has already awarded Rs.10,39,200/-, therefore, claimant would be entitled for enhancement of compensation of Rs.2,57,040/- (Rs.12,96,240/- - Rs.10,39,200/-).

By way of this appeal, appellants are seeking enhancement of Rs.2,00,000/- lacs by paying court fee of Rs.5,000/-.

Annual income Rs.92,400/-
Loss of consortium Rs.96,000/-
(2xRs.48,000/-) 9

(Rs.18,000/- + Rs.18,000/-) 10
